trĭchĭla , ae, f.,
I.a bower, arbor, summer-house, Verg. Copa, 7; Col. poët. 10, 378; 10, 394; Inscr. Orell. 4517; Caes. B. C. 3, 96 (al. triclinia).—Also, in a contr. collat. form ‡ trĭcla , ae, f., Inscr. Orell. 2909: ‡ trĭ-clĕa , ae, ib. 4337; and ‡ trĭclĭa , ae, ib. 4456.dagger; trĭchĭnus , a, um, adj., = τρίχινος (of hair; transf.), slight, meagre, poor: quaestus (opp. uber), Varr. ap. Non. 181, 10.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
